newsitem.title: UK: Japanese stocks in London up, but cautious on dlr.
newsitem.headline: Japanese stocks in London up, but cautious on dlr.

text.p: Japanese stocks in London advanced from Tokyo's close on Friday, but trading was quiet as the market waited to see what course the dollar would take, traders said.

The Nikkei 50 index of leading shares traded in London was at 1,423.54 at 1429 GMT, 25.17 points or 1.74 percent below London's Thursday close, after the Tokyo Nikkei 225 index ended 464.56 points or 2.44 percent lower at 18,557.00.

"It's been pretty quiet," one market-maker said, "Everything went down in early trade on the back of the dollar. The market's not too confident where it'll go from here, but most think it will continue to weaken towards the end of April."
There was some selling in banks and exporters, and some cautious buyers dipped their toes into blue chips, but there was no aggressive trading, he added.
"It seems nobody really cares about the market. People are just trying to stay out of the way."
"Running into April, a lot of money is being repatriated to the yen, so the dollar will probably come under pressure," he said.
Downgrades of some overly-optimistic earnings estimates, based on the dollar trading around 125 yen, also added pressure to the market, traders said.
Toshiba Corp announced a lower-than-expected earning estimate, shaving 40 billion yen off its pre-tax profit estimate to 120 billion yen.
"There is market speculation the dollar/yen is going to drop to 110 yen," the dealer added.
